question: My employer mentions an ROE and Service Canada following a layoff in Canada. What benefits program are they referring to, and must I wait until all paperwork is gathered to apply?
generated_answer: You may be eligible for the EI regular benefits if you have worked and paid EI premiums in the last year and meet the program’s eligibility criteria. The program’s eligibility criteria include, among others, that your layoff was for reasons beyond your control and that you are actively looking for work. You may be eligible for the EI fishing benefits if you are a self-employed fish harvester, and you have worked and paid EI premiums in the last year and meet the program’s eligibility criteria. The program’s eligibility criteria include, among others, that you have a minimum amount of earnings from self-employed fishing, and that your fishing earnings are less than 70% of your maximum insurable earnings for the benefit period. You do not have to wait until all paperwork is gathered to apply for EI regular benefits. However, you must apply for EI regular benefits as soon as you stop working, even if your employer has not yet issued your ROE to you. If you do not apply as soon as you stop working, you may lose benefits. You do not have to wait until all paperwork is gathered to apply for EI fishing benefits. However, you must apply for EI fishing benefits within 30 days of the end of your fishing season, even if you have not yet received your T4 slips. If you do not apply within 30 days, you may lose benefits.
